questions.title: Large-Margin Learning of Submodular Summarization Methods
questions.question: In 'Large-Margin Learning of Submodular Summarization Methods', what type of summarization is trained with the proposed supervised method?
questions.reference_answer: The method trains submodular scoring functions for extractive multi-document summarization.

questions.title: Large-Margin Learning of Submodular Summarization Methods
questions.question: Why does the structural-SVM learning approach in 'Large-Margin Learning of Submodular Summarization Methods' improve on manually tuned summarization models?
questions.reference_answer: It directly learns the scoring parameters and coverage-redundancy trade-off, can handle many features, and significantly outperforms hand-tuned models on DUC 2003 and 2004.

questions.title: Neural Enquirer: Learning to Query Tables with Natural Language
questions.question: In 'Neural Enquirer: Learning to Query Tables with Natural Language', what does the model execute natural-language queries against to obtain answers?
questions.reference_answer: It executes the queries against knowledge-base tables and returns table values as answers.

questions.title: Neural Enquirer: Learning to Query Tables with Natural Language
questions.question: In 'Neural Enquirer: Learning to Query Tables with Natural Language', how does the model handle multi-step compositional queries without predefined logical operations?
questions.reference_answer: It stacks differentiable executors that condition operations on the query and store intermediate table annotations in layered memory, learning their logic end to end from query-answer pairs.

questions.title: Quasi-Recurrent Neural Networks
questions.question: According to the paper 'Quasi-Recurrent Neural Networks', how much faster can QRNNs be than stacked LSTMs?
questions.reference_answer: QRNNs can be up to 16 times faster during training and testing.

questions.title: Quasi-Recurrent Neural Networks
questions.question: In 'Quasi-Recurrent Neural Networks', how do QRNNs combine the useful properties of convolutional and recurrent sequence models?
questions.reference_answer: They compute context-invariant features convolutionally in parallel while using recurrent pooling for long-distance context and sequence order.

questions.title: Neural Symbolic Machines: Learning Semantic Parsers on Freebase with Weak Supervision
questions.question: In 'Neural Symbolic Machines: Learning Semantic Parsers on Freebase with Weak Supervision', what are the two main components of the proposed system?
questions.reference_answer: It combines a neural sequence-to-sequence programmer with key-variable memory and a symbolic Lisp interpreter that executes programs.

aliases: sequence-to-sequence model that maps language utterances to programs and utilizes a key-variable memory

questions.title: Neural Symbolic Machines: Learning Semantic Parsers on Freebase with Weak Supervision
questions.question: In 'Neural Symbolic Machines: Learning Semantic Parsers on Freebase with Weak Supervision', how is training stabilized when only weak supervision is available?
questions.reference_answer: It applies REINFORCE to optimize task reward and bootstraps learning with pseudo-gold programs found through iterative maximum-likelihood training.

questions.title: Describing Videos by Exploiting Temporal Structure
questions.question: Which two mechanisms model local and global temporal structure in 'Describing Videos by Exploiting Temporal Structure'?
questions.reference_answer: A 3-D convolutional neural network models local temporal dynamics, while temporal attention selects relevant segments across the full video.

questions.title: Describing Videos by Exploiting Temporal Structure
questions.question: According to 'Describing Videos by Exploiting Temporal Structure', why can averaging all frame features be inadequate for video description?
questions.reference_answer: Averaging collapses time, can mix distinct events and objects incoherently, and loses information about their order.
required_concepts: fuses temporally distinct events and objects

questions.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with a Combinatorial Action Space for Predicting Popular Reddit Threads
questions.question: In 'Deep Reinforcement Learning with a Combinatorial Action Space for Predicting Popular Reddit Threads', which architecture performed best?
questions.reference_answer: The model using a bidirectional LSTM to represent dependencies among sub-actions performed best.

questions.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with a Combinatorial Action Space for Predicting Popular Reddit Threads
questions.question: In 'Deep Reinforcement Learning with a Combinatorial Action Space for Predicting Popular Reddit Threads', what limitations and future improvements are identified?
questions.reference_answer: Performance remains far below an oracle; future work should incorporate timing and short-term reactions, support backtracking, and address combinatorial complexity more systematically.
